_doc: Interactions (Interactions autoload). Each verb appears in NPC conversations whose role is in 'roles' (civilian, merchant, witness, guard) when 'requires' is met by the PLAYER (flag/any_flag/not_flag, tag = any of the chosen tag ids, age = any bracket, item, min_credits, min_wealth, max_wealth, npc_trait = NPC has any of these traits, goal = motivation goal flag). chance (0-1) + chance_mods: 'npc:<trait>', 'faction:<npc faction>', 'flag:<player flag>', 'tag:<player tag>', 'attitude' (x NPC attitude), 'rep' (x player rep with NPC faction). success/fail: lines (random), effects (Encounters effect DSL + attitude, npc: calm|flee|silenced|informant|follow|angry, rumor, fame, followers, discount, secret), verb = Causality verb recorded (on success unless record_on = fail/always). once = per NPC. Tokens: {npc} {name} {age} {cost} {faction} {heir} {job} {need}.

lines: "Honestly? Nobody's asked me anything in weeks. I'm {job}. It's... a job."
"Small talk is taxed at 3% here, but I'll risk it." They actually smile.
"Did you catch #media_product# last night? #show_opinion#"
"#chatter#" They seem glad somebody listened.
"Know what I miss? #thing.cap#. Before they started billing for it."
"The #team# play tonight. I've got #small_num# credits on them. That's my rent."
"I'm {job}. Don't ask what it pays. It pays in #product#."
"Somebody wrote '#graffiti#' on the wall by my place. I've started to agree with it."
"What do I need? {need}. Same as everyone."
They look at you like nobody has ever asked. "{need}. Can you believe it?"
"What do I need? {need}. And #aspiration#, one day. A person can dream. Dreams are billed, but still."
"...No catch? Is this a prank show?" They pocket it fast, before reality corrects itself.
"I'll pay you back. I won't, but I'll think about it."
They eat like the paste might be repossessed mid-bite. "I owe you. Here's something nobody's supposed to know..."
They go pale and empty their pockets. "Take it. Take it! I have a family. Well, a subscription to one."
"Okay, okay! I don't want trouble. I can't afford trouble."
"Are you threatening me? I have a Paragon panic button and I'm not afraid to subscribe."
They laugh. Actually laugh. That hurts more than a punch.
Your fingers do their little dance. {npc} never feels a thing.
A wallet, a breath mint and a coupon for 5% off air. Not bad.
"HEY! THIEF! Somebody call Paragon! Somebody bill this person!"
Their hand clamps on your wrist. "That's my rent, you absolute ledger."
"Ha! Finally someone says it. They charge for the echo in here, you know."
They lean in. "Keep talking like that and they'll bill you. I like you."
"I'm reporting this to my loyalty-points manager."
"The Consortium feeds my kids. Mostly paste. But still."

recruit_informant.text: Pay them to be your eyes here ({cost} cr)

lines: "Eyes for hire. If anyone radios Paragon about you, I'll 'lose signal'."
"I hear everything on this street. Now you will too."
"Snitch for you? I snitch for Paragon, and they pay in coupons. ...Fine, no." They keep the money.

pull_rank.text: "Do you know who my family is?"

lines: They recognise the {heir} crest and nearly bow into the pavement. "Of course! Whatever you need, it's on the house. Everything is on your house."
"Forgive me, I didn't recognise the - the jawline. Very {heir}."
"Your family? Your family owns my debt. So yes. I know who they are." They spit near your shoes.
"Rich kid wandering the gutter? Somebody call Lumen, this is content."
They stare at the number. Then at you. "I... could buy air for a year."
"Is this real? This is real. I never saw you. I never saw anything. I'm going to buy a window."

call_lawyer.text: Have the family lawyer call them

lines: Your lawyer's hologram flickers on. Forty seconds later {npc} has signed an NDA, a non-compete and a non-memory clause.
"Under clause 9 of the Witness Courtesy Act, you saw nothing," the lawyer purrs. They agree. Everybody agrees.
The lawyer's hologram buffers. And buffers. "Your subscription has lapsed," it says, and vanishes.
They fish out a coin. "Don't spend it on air. ...Okay, spend it on air."
"Here. Don't tell anyone I'm soft. It's bad for my credit score."
"Get a job." They have two. Neither pays.
They walk past you like you're an ad they've already skipped.
"You hear things down here, right? Me too. Swap?"
Gossip is the only currency the Consortium hasn't taxed. Yet.
"I don't talk to gutter people." They say it from about one paycheck away.
You become one more grey shape under the ads. {npc} blinks. "Where... I swear someone was right there."
"Nice try, gutter-ghost. I've got your face on my retina cache."
They scan you. "Oh - you're PROPERTY. Property can't commit crimes, legally. My mistake."
"Collateral, huh." Their face softens. "Me too. Section 4, sub-asset 12. Go on."
"Property that misbehaves gets repossessed. I'm calling your owner."
"For that much I'd follow you into a black hole. Do you need anyone followed into a black hole?"
They sign a loyalty contract you wrote on a napkin. It is legally binding. Everything is.
You do the eyes. The big ones. "Aw. Kids today. Go on, run home before the curfew billing starts."
"You? A criminal? You're barely billable."
"Don't 'mister' me, I've seen kids repo a whole freighter."
"Don't tell your parents. Or my parents. Or my bank."
They sigh and hand you a few credits. "Buy something that isn't paste."
"Pocket money? I'M still waiting for MY pocket money."
"Of course, sir or madam or esteemed relic. Fifteen percent off, and a free ad."
They check your face, then the law. The law, grudgingly, agrees.
"The senior discount was discontinued for being too popular with seniors."

back_in_my_day.text: Tell them how things were back in your day

lines: "...Free air? Unbilled rain? Is that true?" They listen until they forget whatever they were about to do. Including the phone call.
By the time you reach the part about public parks, they're crying a little. "I didn't know it could be different."
"Yeah, yeah, and you walked to work uphill both ways in zero-G."
Their eyes glaze over. They hold up a finger, still on hold with Paragon.

remember_old_world.text: Describe the world before the Consortium

lines: You describe the sky with no ads. {npc} goes quiet. "Where would someone even go to find that again?" A spark. A dangerous one.
You clean, stitch, bandage. "No invoice? No... invoice?" They hold your hand a second too long.
"Halcyon wanted 400 for that. You did it with gum and a smile."
Ten seconds of glowing glyphs. Their Paragon call drops, their balance drops, and their wallpaper is now you.
You slip into their wristpad. Credit, contacts, and a very embarrassing search history.
Their firewall bites back. Your deck smokes. "Did you just try to HACK me?"
"Officer! I didn't - I was just calling to report... my own enthusiasm for compliance."
They see the visor logo and snap to attention. Nobody checks the expiry date. Nobody ever does.
"That badge expired in 3029. Impersonating an officer is a premium-tier crime."
"...pursuant to sub-clause 14, your memory of this event is the intellectual property of my client." They nod, terrified, and delete it.
You cite three statutes, two of which you invented. They fold.
"I have a lawyer too." They do. He's worse than you. This could take years.
"Air belongs to everyone," you say. {npc} repeats it, quietly, like a password. They'll be back - with friends.
Something lights up behind their eyes. "Where do I sign? Wait - nothing to sign? That's the most beautiful thing I've ever heard."
"Free air? Sounds like a scam. A good scam, but a scam."
You talk wages, hours, air. By the end they've signed your card in invisible ink. "When it starts, I'm in."
"Unions are illegal on Tuesdays. And it's always Tuesday."
You go live. {npc} becomes a meme in eleven seconds and loves every bit of it. "Tell my mum!"
The chat explodes. 40,000 bots and three real people. One of them sends a tip.
"Turn that off! I'm in witness protection! Well, witness subscription!"
You turn grey paste into something that smells like a memory. They eat, and for a minute they're somewhere else.
"What IS this?" Paste. With love. And a dangerous amount of chilli.
The dice land. You win. They pay, swearing in three corporate dialects.
"Again?" they ask. You never say no to again.
Snake eyes. Your credits leave you like they always do.
"Unlicensed? Untaxed? ...It smells like a forest. Two, please."
They inhale. Real air. Their eyes water. "Where do you GET this?"
"Smuggled air? I'm OxyGenix Loyal Tier! I'm calling it in!"
Old habits. You scan their implants for missed payments and find one. They hand over a gadget, shaking.
"Halcyon said it was mine for life!" Halcyon defines 'life' as 'until Tuesday'.
"You don't work for Halcyon anymore. I checked. EVERYONE checked."

deliver_message.text: Offer to carry a message for them

lines: "Could you get this to my sister on another planet? Paragon reads all the mail." You pocket it. You never look inside.
They hand you a sealed note and a coin. "Fastest courier in the Sprawl, they say."
Your eyes flicker binary. Their implant agrees to forget. "Have a compliant day," it says, in their voice.
Machine to machine. Their wristpad decides it likes you more than it likes them.
"Did your eyes just go blue? Are you a - are you OFFICE EQUIPMENT?"
"Colony 9? Cell block D? ...Brother. Sister. Whatever. You're family." They tell you everything.
They don't get it. Then they do, and they back away slowly.
Thirty seconds and you've written them a theme song. They'll hum it until they die, which in the Sprawl is soon.
"♪ {npc}, {npc}, worth every credit! ♪" A merchant two stalls down offers to buy the rights.
"Is that... the OxyGenix jingle with my name in it? I'm calling legal."

bouncer_escort.text: Offer to walk them home safely

lines: Nobody bothers someone walking next to you. At their door they press a coin into your hand and a secret into your ear.
"Well. Aren't you a breath of fresh, unlicensed air."
They laugh at your joke before you finish it. You could ask for anything. You ask for a little.
"Is that a line? That's a line. I've heard better from vending machines."

extort.text: Make them an offer they can't refuse

lines: You explain, calmly, what happens to people who don't pay protection. They pay protection.
"Every week?" Every week. They nod like someone signing their own repo papers.
"I already pay protection. To Paragon. They'll want to meet you."
You tell them exactly what you did and why. Nobody has told them the truth in years. They hang up on Paragon.
"That's... the most honest thing I've heard since the Consortium patented honesty."
"Thanks for the confession. Paragon gives a bonus for those."

plead.text: Beg them not to hurt you

lines: You grovel with a sincerity that would win awards. They pity you so hard they forget what they were doing.
"Get up, get up. You're making me feel like a shareholder."
"Pathetic. This is going on Lumen."
One shove becomes a brawl. You win. You always win. Someone pays you to stop.
Fists, then apologies, then they buy you a drink. Hotheads understand each other.
They hit back harder than expected. You both lie in the street, billing each other for medical.
You both read the billboard aloud in the voice of a dying robot. It's the best five minutes they've had all year.
"'Breathe Responsibly'? I breathe IRRESPONSIBLY." They're crying laughing.
"Shh! The billboard can hear you. It has a loyalty programme."
You don't promise anything. You just say it out loud. They stand a little straighter. "Yeah. Yeah, maybe."
"If someone like you still believes it..." They hang up the Paragon call. "...then I can too."
"Change? The last guy who said that got repossessed. By his own shoes."
"How many OxyGenix execs does it take to change a light? None - they bill you for the dark." They wheeze. The phone call is forgotten.
Your joke is so bad it loops back to good. They're laughing too hard to report anything.
Silence. A billboard laughs instead, pre-recorded. Somehow that's worse.
You tell them you're an undercover Lumen producer filming 'Compliance Heroes'. They thank you. They want an autograph.
Your lie is so detailed it has footnotes. They believe every one.
"Your story has a plot hole. I'm a plot-hole inspector. Licensed."
They squint. "Same eyes as you... I saw someone like that. Heading off-world, in a Halcyon transport."
"Yeah! Worked the vats with them. They talked about a sibling in cryo. Said they'd find you first."
"Sorry. Everyone looks the same after a few years of paste."

ask_love.text: Ask if they've seen the one you lost

lines: "Wedding ring like that? There's someone at the docks who wears the twin. Never takes it off. Never talks about it."
"Everyone's lost someone. Here they bill you for the grief."

ai_whisper.text: Let the ghost in your head do the talking

lines: Your mouth says things you didn't plan, in a voice like a customer-service chime. It works. It always works. That's what scares you.
The ghost quotes their own purchase history back at them. They hand over whatever it asks for.
"Why did your voice just glitch? Why did you say my mother's maiden name?"
"...The paste is warm tonight," you say. Their eyes widen. "And the air is never free." A fellow agent. Which side? Does it matter?
"Why are you telling me the paste is warm? It's always warm. That's the problem."
"...How long?" Not long. They take your hand. Whatever they were about to do, they don't.
They give you their last air canister. You try to refuse. They insist.
"Halcyon can finance your funeral. Want their number?"
At the word 'Syndicate' they go very still. "I don't want any trouble with... them." Neither do you, honestly.
"The Syndicate? They're looking for YOU, friend. There's a reward."
"Fine! Fine. You drive a harder bargain than Halcyon. Ten percent off."
"You're robbing me. Legally. I respect it."
"Haggling? That's a premium feature." The price goes UP.
A medkit migrates from the counter to your pocket. The merchant is busy arguing with an ad.
You browse. You 'browse'. Your pockets are heavier.
"Put. It. Back." They've seen a thousand shoplifters. You were number one thousand and one.
"...Fine. Maybe it wasn't what it looked like. #after_talk_ok#"
They listen. Really listen. "Okay. I'll let it go. This once."
"Self-defence, huh? On {planet} everything's self-defence. Alright."
"I know what I saw."
"Save it for Paragon." #judge_disapprove#
"Explanations are cheap. #faction# taught me that."

hush_money.text: Slip them {cost} credits to forget it

lines: The credits vanish. So does the memory. "Saw what? I've been staring at a billboard all day."
"Forget what? I've got a terrible memory. It's a medical condition. Thanks for the treatment."
"#small_num# seconds ago? I was asleep. Standing up. It's a talent."

spread_the_word.text: Ask them to tell people what they saw

lines: "Oh, I'm telling EVERYONE. My cousin has #small_num# followers."
"By tonight the whole queue at the noodle stall will know."
"Leave it with me. Gossip is the one thing #faction# can't tax."
"And get on Paragon's list? No thanks."
"I'll keep that one to myself, if it's all the same."
They try it. They nail it. "I'm going to dodge my landlord so hard."
"Like this? LIKE THIS?" Close enough. They're delighted.
Two tries, one bruise, one triumph. "Teach me more next time!"
They try it. They fall over. "...I'll stick to standing still."
"My knees are on a payment plan. Maybe later."

ask_reputation.text: Ask what people say about you

lines: They lean in.
"You want the truth? Okay."
They glance at the nearest drone, then whisper.
"An apology? On {planet}? I need to sit down."
"...Okay. Thanks. Nobody says sorry here. It's not in the contract."
They soften. "We all have bad days. Yours are just louder."
"Sorry doesn't pay for the damage."
"Tell it to #faction#."
For one song, nobody's billing anybody. "#judge_amused#"
They spin, you spin, a drone films it. "Worth it."
"I haven't danced since #time#... last year." They're laughing.
"Dancing is billed by the minute here."
They step back. "I'll watch. Watching is free."

ask_patch_up.text: Ask them to help patch you up

lines: They tear a strip off a promo banner. "Hold still. #brand# makes great bandages."
"My mum was a medic. Sort of. She watched a lot of #media_product#." It helps anyway.
A spray of something minty, a bandage, a pat. "Don't bleed on my street again."
"I faint at blood. And at medical bills."
"Clinic's that way. I'm not liable."
"You think THAT was something? Let me tell you about the paste riot of '#small_num#."
They roll up a sleeve: a scar shaped like a #brand# logo. "Repo drone. Long story."
"Respect. My grandad took down a #faction# convoy with a shopping trolley."

ask_cover.text: Ask them to cover for you

lines: "Paragon asks, you were at the noodle stall with me. All night."
"Cover for you? I'll lie to their faces. It's my hobby."
"We look after our own here. You're our own now."
"I like you. I don't like you THAT much."
"I've got a family. Sort of. No."

one_on_one.text: Run a quick one-on-one with them

lines: You ask about their goals. They cry a little. "Nobody's ever asked. #after_talk_ok#"
"Strengths? Surviving. Weaknesses? Also surviving." You give them 'exceeds expectations'. They glow.
Ten minutes, one action item, zero layoffs. "Best meeting I've ever had."
"Is this a performance review? Am I being let go from the street?"
"Let's circle back. Never."
"Accept, decline, accept - the algorithm thinks you're desperate and pays more." You trade a trick back. Both of you earn.
"Never rate the customer below four. They rate you back." Solid. You split a surge bonus.
They show you a dead zone where the delivery app can't track tips. Free money. Sort of.
"My hacks are my pension. Get your own."
You compare air bills. Theirs is worse. You both laugh until you cough. "Same time next week?"
"#thing.cap# went up again." "Mine too." A whole friendship, built on invoices.
They share a trick: breathe in the stairwell, it's billed at the residential rate.
"It's the same year it was yesterday, friend. Cryo-brain?" They explain #absurd_policy_lower# like it's normal. It is now.
They tell you the year. You do the maths. Your debt is older than they are.
"You slept through #small_num# price hikes. Lucky."
Page #small_num#, clause 9: illegal. You circle it. They stare at you like you just handed them a planet.
"You found WHAT in the small print?" Halcyon owes THEM #small_num# credits. Technically. Legally. Hilariously.
You explain compound interest. They sit down on the kerb. Then they get angry. Good angry.
The contract is a 400-page hologram that refuses to scroll.

show_crystal.text: Show them a real asteroid crystal

lines: It catches the neon and throws it everywhere. "Is that... real? Nothing here is real."
"From the belt? You dug that out yourself?" They hold it like a baby. They give it back. Barely.
A crowd of three forms. Then six. Rocks are rare when everything is plastic.

ask_my_face.text: Ask if they've seen your face before

lines: "Your face? Yeah - on a #brand# ad. Different hair. Happier."
"There's a guy at the paste plant with your face. He's nicer."
They squint. "#num# of you came through last month. You're the only one who asked."

paste_truth.text: Tell them what's really in the paste

lines: You tell them. They look at their lunch. They put down their lunch. "...Thank you. I think."
"Batch 88? THE Batch 88?" Word will spread by dinner. If anyone still eats dinner.
You keep it vague. 'Protein.' 'Mostly.' 'Ethically sourced, legally speaking.' They get the idea.
"I don't want to know. I'm on a payment plan for my stomach."
"Unloading air trucks at #time#. No questions. No breaks. No lungs left after." You get a tip-off and a taste of pay.
"Paste plant needs tasters. #small_num# credits a spoon." You do one shift on the spot.
They pay you to stand in their queue. An hour of standing: honest money.
"Not my business. Not yours either."
They shrug. "Ask someone braver."
"Burn the Consortium? ...I've got matches. And a cousin with more matches."
They look at the nearest billboard for a long time. "Count me in. Quietly."
"Finally. I've been waiting for someone to say it out loud."
"Not my business. Not yours either."
They shrug. "Ask someone braver."
They film. You perform. #small_num# views in a minute. "You're going to be huge!"
"Say something quotable!" You do. It's already a sticker by tonight.
The clip goes round the block before you've finished talking.
"Not my business. Not yours either."
They shrug. "Ask someone braver."

goal_tycoon.text: Ask what they'd want from the owner of a planet

lines: "Free air. A window. A day off. In that order." You take notes. Real notes.
"A planet where the ads ask permission." They're smiling. "You'd do that?"
"Honestly? Just don't bill us for the sky."

goal_revenge.text: Ask about the one you're hunting

lines: They go quiet. Then they tell you everything they know.
"Revenge, huh? Good. Somebody should." They lower their voice.
"I didn't tell you this."
"Not my business. Not yours either."
They shrug. "Ask someone braver."

goal_cure.text: Ask about clinics and miracle cures

lines: "The clinic on the corner waters down the good stuff. Ask for the back room." They press a blister pack into your hand.
"My aunt swore by a fortune teller's tonic. My aunt also died." Still, they give you something for the pain.
"Real medicine? On {planet}?" But they know a guy. They always know a guy.
"Not my business. Not yours either."
They shrug. "Ask someone braver."

goal_family.text: Ask them to pass a message home

lines: "My cousin flies the freight run. Your message will get there." Something in your chest loosens.
They promise. You believe them. That's rare here.
"Family first. Always." They write it on their hand.
Thirty seconds, four buzzwords, one dream. "I'd invest. If I had credits. Or a future."
"Disrupt the air market? Ha!" But they're listening. "...Go on."
They ask for a job. You've got your first employee. Unpaid. Like a real CEO.
"Not my business. Not yours either."
They shrug. "Ask someone braver."
"Freighters leave from the east docks at #time#. Stowaways ride free. Mostly."
"Everybody wants out. Nobody gets out." But they tell you about a smuggler with a soft heart.
They point at the sky. "That light? That's the way out. Follow the debt freighters."

goal_redemption.text: Do them a small kindness, no strings ({cost} cr)

lines: You fix a strap, carry a bag, listen to a story. Small things. They remember small things.
You pay their noodle tab and walk away before they can thank you.
"Why?" Because. They don't get it. They'll remember it.
"Nice to meet you, uh... that." When Paragon asks, they'll describe someone else entirely.
Your other name rolls off your tongue like you were born with it. They'll never connect the two.
"Funny, you don't look like a {name}." Exactly.

real_air.text: Ask where to breathe something real

lines: "Rooftop garden behind the karaoke place. Real plants. Real-ish air." Your sinuses weep with joy.
"Stand by the hydroponics vent at #time#. Smells like rain did when I was a kid."
They hand you a hanky that smells of actual grass. You don't ask.
You tell them you once sold air back to OxyGenix. They believe every word. Half of it was even true.
Your story has a hijacked billboard, a duck and a duel. By the end they're cheering.
"No WAY." Yes way. Well, no. But they'll tell it for years.
"Sure. And I'm the CEO of Lumen."
They've heard better lies from the billboards.

sleeper_phrase.text: Recite the phrase that isn't yours

lines: Their pupils go wide. They answer with the second half of the phrase. Neither of you knows who taught it to you.
"...The paste is warm in winter." They answer: "And colder in the vats." You both pretend that didn't happen. They'll protect you now.
They stare at you. "Are you... okay?"
"Is that a jingle? I don't know that jingle."

give_back.text: Give back the thing you 'found' in their pocket

lines: "My lucky charm! Where did you - you know what, I don't want to know. Thank you!"
You hand back a lighter, a ration card and a photo. They didn't notice it was gone. They do notice it's back.
"Huh. You're the most honest thief I've ever met."
Something in the way you stand. They bow before they know why.
"You're... related to somebody, aren't you? Somebody up there." They won't breathe a word.
Old blood has a voice. Yours speaks. They listen.
They squint. "Nope. You're nobody. Same as me."

ask_the_dead.text: Ask if the dead ever leave them alone

lines: "My dad visits in dreams. Still asks about his debt." You both stand in the quiet for a moment.
"They don't. You learn to set a place for them." They don't ask who yours are.
"On {planet}? The dead get billed too. They leave eventually."
"What kind of question is that?" They back away.

borrow_life.text: Borrow a few details of their life

lines: Birthday, first pet, mother's maiden name. All in casual chat. Your next identity is getting richer.
They tell you everything a security question would ask. You smile. You remember.
"Why do you want to know my first pet's name?" They know that trick.

poor: A bed that isn't rented by the hour
Someone to pay off my water debt
worker: A boss who goes missing. Permanently
Shoes that don't belong to Halcyon
artsy: Ten minutes of silence, no ads
A muse. Or rent. Rent first
Someone to buy my soul at a fair price
corporate: A promotion before my clone gets it
Three more loyalty points for Platinum
Someone to blame for the quarterly
A way out that doesn't void my pension
rebel: A broadcast slot Lumen doesn't control
My cell-mate out of a Paragon colony
Proof the Consortium lies. More proof
A ship that doesn't phone home
weird: The sky to stop humming at me
To know what's in the paste. Really

5: "Is that a {heir} crest? Oh. OH. Can I... get you anything? Anything at all?"
"Rich people don't come down here. Unless they're lost. Or buying the street."
4: "Nice coat. Real fabric? I could live a month on one sleeve."
"You smell like money. Old money. The kind that doesn't pay for air."
3: "Executive type, huh? Here to 'experience the street'? It costs extra."
"You've got that corner-office posture. My spine is jealous."
2: "Another middle-tier soul. Hanging on, like the rest of us."
"You look like you approve expense reports. Approve mine?"
1: "Rough shift? You look like a rough shift."
"Hey, I know that look. Two jobs, no sleep. Same."
0: "You sleep under the ad-bridge too? I think I've seen you there."
"Careful, Paragon sweeps this corner for people who look like us."

teen: "Shouldn't you be in a learning-subscription somewhere, kid?"
"Kids these days. Already in debt. Respect."
elder: "Respect your elders, they said. Then they billed the elders."
"You remember when air was free, grandparent? Tell me it was real."
ancient: "You're... really old. Like, museum old. Are you on loan?"
"Is it true you were born before the Consortium? What was it like?"

warm: "Hey, you look like one of us. Rough century, huh?"
"Finally, someone who doesn't smell like a shareholder."
"You've got kind eyes. Rare. Probably illegal."
"You look like you need #dish#. The stall on the corner does a good one."
"Stay out of trouble. Or at least out of #faction#'s."
cold: "Don't stand so close, you'll lower my credit score."
"Whatever you're selling, I already owe on it."
"Unless you're buying, I'm busy. Busy owing."
"Move along. I'm on the clock. The clock belongs to #faction#."
neutral: "Breathe quietly, friend. They bill by the decibel now."
"Got any spare air? No? Yeah. Nobody does."
"Don't look at the ads too long. They look back."
"Careful. #pa_body.cap#" They shrug. "That's what the speakers say, anyway."

saga: "Someone called {ally} has been asking around {objective_planet} about {macguffin}. Sounds like trouble. The fun kind."
